name: WHO Global Health Observatory (JMP)
covers: Population using at least basic and safely managed drinking water and sanitation, basic handwashing facilities, and WASH-attributable mortality, by country and by urban/rural residence, 2000-2024
note: OData API, no key and no account. WHO's publication of the WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme estimates. Read as the main source because it splits urban from rural, which the World Bank's copy does not.

name: World Bank World Development Indicators
covers: The same JMP series (SH.H2O.BASW.ZS, SH.H2O.SMDW.ZS, SH.STA.BASS.ZS, SH.STA.SMSS.ZS, SH.STA.HYGN.ZS, SH.STA.ODFC.ZS), plus population (SP.POP.TOTL), region and income group
note: No key. Used for the cross-check, for population, and as the source of open defecation, which GHO publishes at country level only as a whole-percent string.

name: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme
covers: The originating estimates behind both APIs above
note: Cited for provenance. Neither API is read as an independent measurement of the world: they are two publications of one set of JMP estimates, and the cross-check between them verifies that the copies agree, not that the estimates are right.

name: UN Sustainable Development Goal 6
covers: The definition of target 6.1 and of indicator 6.1.1, safely managed drinking water
note: The target is universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water for all by 2030. Indicator 6.1.1 is the safely-managed share used throughout this page.
